title: Workload fingerprinting and runtime advisor for attention kernels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a lightweight workload fingerprinting layer and a runtime advisor that recommends an attention kernel and prefill/decode schedule for each request pattern. The advisor should be low-latency (<=1ms added p99 per request), explainable, and safe: it must provide a conservative fallback when confidence is low or memory pressure is detected. This ticket covers design, implementation of the fingerprint collector, offline model for heuristic scoring, an in-runtime advisory API, and a canary rollout plan with rollback guards.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint metadata collected for >=95% of routed attention requests in canary cluster
Advisor API returns kernel recommendation + confidence score within 1ms p99 for 99% of advisory lookups
Canary runs demonstrate no P0 regressions; p95 latency and error rate remain within canary SLOs
Automatic fallback to conservative kernel occurs when confidence < 0.3 or GPU free memory < threshold
Documentation and runbook created for interpreting advisor recommendations and performing manual overrides
technical_notes: Fingerprint fields: model_family, sequence_length, batch_shape_signature, token_density, prefix_hit_rate, kv_cache_hit_estimate, quantization_profile, recent_latency_ms, memory_peak_delta
Design choice: keep fingerprint small (<=256 bytes) and sampled at 1% for full traces to limit dp/telemetry risk
Scoring model: gradient-boosted heuristics derived from offline microbench corpus + hand-tuned shims for known edgecases (extremely long prefixes, tiny microbatches)
Advisor integration points: request ingress (for prefill path) and decoder scheduler (for decode path). Advisory hook must be optional and controllable by route config
Safety: advisor must not block request flow; failures are treated as 'no recommendation' and fall back to existing kernel-selection logic
plan: Week 1: implement lightweight fingerprint collector and schema; add sampling toggle and storage in trace context
Week 2: run offline microbench suite to populate scoring table across common sequence distributions and model families (Llama2, Mistral, Mixtral variants)
Week 3: implement runtime advisor service and local in-process cache for recommendations; add feature flag gating
Week 4: run closed canary (internal services) with traffic split 100% -> 1% advisory, monitor sentinel metrics
Week 5: expand canary to external beta customers, collect regressions, iterate heuristics, add automatic rollback triggers
testing_plan: Synthetic microbench: grid over seq_len {8,32,64,128,512,1024} x batch_size {1,2,4,8} x kv_cache_hit {0,50,90}%
Long-tail stress: mix of prefix-heavy workloads with intermittent large-decoder bursts to observe memory pressure and advisory stability
Regression harness: run against existing flash-like kernels and v3-equivalent kernels to ensure advisor doesn't increase p95 by >5% compared to baseline
A/B: route 50/50 in staging between advisor-enabled and advisor-disabled paths, capture token cost delta, GPU utilization, and error rates
rollout_plan: Feature flagged rollout per cluster: dev -> staging -> internal-canary -> external-canary -> general availability
Canary metrics: p95 latency, tail OOMs, token throughput, and customer error signals. Thresholds: p95 increase >7% or new OOMs -> immediate rollback
Automatic rollback: integrate with rollout orchestrator; advisor toggles must be revertible via single flag flip
Manual override: route-level configuration to pin kernel selection for critical customers
observability: New metrics: advisor_recommendation_total, advisor_confidence_histogram, advisor_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, advisor_fallbacks_total
Dashboards: per-model-family heatmap of recommended kernel vs observed decay in performance
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: advisor misclassification causing p99 regressions under rare memory patterns. Mitigation: conservative confidence threshold and immediate fallback on memory signals
Risk: telemetry volume growth from fingerprinting. Mitigation: sample rate control and compact schema; store sampled traces in cold storage only
Risk: interaction with autoscaler (Dedicated) leading to oscillation. Mitigation: smooth recommendations over time and expose advisory smoothing window to autoscaler
